lesson.scenario: A read replica falls behind a primary while a reporting client requires a bounded-staleness read.
entities: Measures time, bytes, and log positions

steps.title: Caught up
steps.narration: Primary and replica are both at LSN 850.
steps.outcome: The reporting replica can satisfy the freshness bound.
steps.invariant: Lag must be measured against an authoritative progress marker.

steps.title: Write burst
steps.narration: The primary commits fifty new log records through LSN 900.
steps.outcome: Replica lag grows while writes continue.
steps.invariant: Lag can be expressed in time, bytes, or log positions; each answers a different question.

steps.title: Apply bottleneck
steps.narration: The stream delivers records, but replay reaches only LSN 860.
steps.outcome: Transport progress does not imply apply progress.
steps.invariant: A freshness check should use replayed state, not merely received bytes.

steps.title: Bound enforced
steps.narration: The monitor routes the report to the primary because lag exceeds two seconds.
steps.outcome: The client avoids an unexpectedly stale replica read.
steps.invariant: A bounded-staleness policy must fail over or reject when its bound cannot be met.

steps.title: Replica recovers
steps.narration: Replay catches up through LSN 900 and the monitor restores replica routing.
steps.outcome: Read scaling resumes after measured recovery.
steps.invariant: Low current lag does not guarantee a future maximum without capacity headroom.
